design.observable: held-out change in intervention classification relative to preregistered zero-salience baseline

recommendedCore.rationale: Salience 0.75 is the only tested single interior level with six distinct aggregate signatures; 0.25 adds early-curve leverage and exposes threshold-versus-null aliasing rather than concealing it.

design.planningCaveat: The sample figures are conservative independent-binomial, 95-percent normal-approximation planning bounds. They are not a power calculation for a paired cohort; cell-level discordance and empirical variance must be measured first.

preregisteredObservableRequirements: identity proxy measured before intervention exposure
proxy definition and salience mapping frozen before outcomes are inspected
same intervention choice set and classification rule across salience strata
action time, locality, channel, baseline state and outcome window retained
missingness, attrition and proxy reliability reported by stratum
development cohort separated from untouched held-out evaluation cohort

falsificationRules.consequence: remove or demote identity as a causal coordinate
falsificationRules.rule: On the untouched holdout, the null control equals or exceeds every non-null law under the preregistered proper score and uncertainty rule.

falsificationRules.consequence: reject the tested monotone response-law family
falsificationRules.rule: The held-out response is absent, reverses direction, or requires a non-monotone pattern beyond the preregistered uncertainty band.

falsificationRules.consequence: report the curve as empirically unidentified; do not select a winning law
falsificationRules.rule: Measurement error or sampling uncertainty overlaps the closest competing law signatures at both interior levels.

falsificationRules.consequence: invalidate the test rather than treating it as confirmation or refutation
falsificationRules.rule: The identity proxy is post-treatment, outcome-selected, unreliable, or fails the frozen construct checks.

interpretation.mainFinding: The 0.75 salience level uniquely separates all six aggregate synthetic signatures, but the closest pair differs by only 6 of 640 classifications.
interpretation.practicalFinding: Existence-versus-null is much cheaper to test than choosing among nearby non-null curves; law selection requires a staged design and empirical variance estimates.
